./packages/flutter_monaco/doc/focus-and-platform-views.md:3:This guide explains how focus and keyboard input work when embedding Monaco in Flutter via platform views (WKWebView on macOS/iOS, WebView2 on Windows, an iframe on Web), what the package does about it on each platform, and what remains a real platform limitation.
./packages/flutter_monaco/doc/focus-and-platform-views.md:9:When typing into Monaco inside a platform view, three layers of focus must align:
./packages/flutter_monaco/doc/focus-and-platform-views.md:15:3) DOM focus (Monaco)
./packages/flutter_monaco/doc/focus-and-platform-views.md:16:    - Inside the web page, Monaco's hidden `textarea.inputarea` (or `.native-edit-context`) must be `document.activeElement`; otherwise typing does not enter the editor.
./packages/flutter_monaco/doc/focus-and-platform-views.md:38:- `MonacoController.requestFocus()` moves real Win32 keyboard focus to WebView2 before focusing Monaco; a pointer-route coordinator returns focus to Flutter when you click Flutter UI, and enforces that a focused Flutter text input takes native focus back.
./packages/flutter_monaco/doc/focus-and-platform-views.md:46:- Keyboard: web's layer-2 "native focus" is the parent document's focus. While the iframe element is the parent `document.activeElement`, every key event dispatches inside the iframe's document and Flutter receives nothing. `setInteractionEnabled(false)` and `releaseNativeFocus()` therefore perform a two-sided handoff: blur Monaco inside the iframe AND move the parent document's focus onto the editor's `<flutter-view>` host, so overlays get Escape/Tab/typing without needing a first click.
./packages/flutter_monaco/doc/focus-and-platform-views.md:50:Also note: while Monaco holds document focus on web, app-global key handlers (`HardwareKeyboard` handlers, `Shortcuts` on ancestors) do not fire - keys never leave the iframe. If the app needs global shortcuts to work while typing in the editor, they must be registered as Monaco keybindings and forwarded over the bridge.
./packages/flutter_monaco/doc/focus-and-platform-views.md:60:- `MonacoFocusIntent.user` - the user directly interacted with the editor (e.g. a primary pointer-down inside it). The package may release a stale Flutter text-input client (`TextInput.hide` + unfocus), perform the native handoff, and focus Monaco.
./packages/flutter_monaco/doc/focus-and-platform-views.md:71:`MonacoEditor` already routes pointer-downs this way with the correct button guards (primary button only; right-clicks never nudge focus, so Monaco's context menu is not torn down).
./packages/flutter_monaco/doc/focus-and-platform-views.md:104:    // Never nudge on right/middle click: it tears down Monaco's context

./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:19:This repository ships an optional, package-specific plugin for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. ./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:470:Flutter Monaco can connect the editor to a **real language server** using Monaco's built-in LSP client (Monaco 0.55+). ./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:572:- **Server markdown is untrusted.** Since Monaco 0.56, hovers, completion documentation, signature help, and inlay-hint tooltips from a language server render `command:` links as plain text and strip inline HTML styling; `http`, `https`, `mailto`, and `file` links still work.
./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:573:- **Document URIs matter.** Language servers key their state on document URIs - open documents with stable `file:///...` URIs (`openDocument(..., uri: ...)`) instead of relying on Monaco's default `inmemory://` model.
./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:574:- **Diagnostics owner.** LSP diagnostics appear as Monaco markers under the owner `'lsp'`; they're cleared automatically when the last connection closes.
./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:575:- **Multiple servers.** Allowed, but Monaco synchronizes *all* models to every connected server and all LSP diagnostics share one marker owner - prefer one server per editor unless your servers handle disjoint files.
./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:610:- Ctrl/meta wheel (editor `mouseWheelZoom`, browser zoom, macOS pinch) is never handed off, and Monaco-owned scrollable overlays (suggest list, hover docs, menus, peek editors) keep their own wheel handling.
./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:633:This is **edge scroll handoff, not native nested scrolling**. Monaco lives inside a WebView/iframe, so the platform gesture itself never enters Flutter's gesture arena; the package forwards the unconsumed scroll intent across the bridge instead. Wheel and trackpad input is the stable, supported source on macOS, Windows, and desktop web (plus external mice on mobile where the WebView reports wheel events).
./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:635:Touch forwarding is a separate, **experimental** opt-in (`mobileTouch: true`). It is observation-only: it never blocks Monaco's own touch handling, never opens the keyboard, and yields to text selection, but there is no native momentum or fling transfer, and iOS Safari on Flutter Web remains best-effort. Under the default boundary policy a drag that starts over scrollable editor content belongs to the editor for its whole lifetime (it is contained at the edge); only a drag that starts while the editor is already at the edge scrolls the page.

./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:1170:On Flutter Web, Monaco is hosted in an `iframe`. The browser routes pointer events inside that iframe to its own document first, so Flutter widgets that visually sit on top of the editor can appear correctly but never receive clicks or drags.
./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:1237:On web, the boundary creates a transparent DOM `<div>` over the widget's global bounds with maximum z-index, and disables pointer events on any intersecting Monaco iframe while the user is hovering or pressing the overlay. ./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:1275:- **Bridge JavaScript is real files.** The editor bridge ships as plain `.js` assets (`assets/monaco/bridge/`), not Dart string literals. The host HTML is generated internally and rewritten on every load, so a package upgrade can never serve a stale bridge.

./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:1296:- **Web**: Native iframe-based integration with Monaco assets served from Flutter's asset bundle
./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:1307:- **Workers**: Monaco's language services (JSON, CSS, HTML, TypeScript/JavaScript) and diff computation run in Web Workers, off the editor's main thread. On a `file://` page whose WebView cannot start them (Windows, only when its virtual host is unavailable), diffs are computed on the main thread and the built-in language services are off.
./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:1323:- The editor page's origin is `https://flutter-monaco.example`, a secure context. Endpoints in `allowedConnectSources` should use `wss://` or `https://`, or `ws://`/`http://` on loopback (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). Listing any other `ws://` or `http://` endpoint, or a bare `*`, makes the editor load from `file://` instead, where Monaco's workers cannot run.
./packages/flutter_monaco/README.md:1344:On web, the Monaco Editor runs inside an iframe that must be mounted in the DOM before initialization can complete. This means you should **not** create a controller and await `whenReady` before the widget tree is built (e.g., in `initState`).

./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:8:Flutter 3.47 moved Material out of the SDK into the `material_ui` package, and flutter_monaco follows it; that type move is the only source-breaking change. The release also upgrades the bundled engine to Monaco 0.57.0, makes Monaco's background workers run on Windows (#43), and fixes a set of bridge, lifecycle, and LSP defects found in a full audit. The README's "Migrating from 3.x to 4.0" section has the short upgrade path.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:13:- **Calls that used to fail silently now throw.** `executeAction` throws for an action or command id that Monaco does not register and for a command that fails, instead of reporting success. Seven `MonacoAction` catalog constants that standalone Monaco does not register are deprecated: `accessibilityHelp`, `accessibleView`, `goToLocation`, `inlineSuggestTriggerInlineEdit`, `inlineSuggestTriggerInlineEditExplicit`, `toggleScreenReaderAccessibilityMode`, and `toggleWordWrap` (set `EditorOptions.wordWrap` with `updateOptions` instead). `executeAction` with a command id, `scrollToTop`, and `scrollToBottom` throw when no document is attached. `getTheme`, `getSelection`, `getCursorPosition`, `document.isDirty()`, and `getWordAt()` throw `MonacoProtocolError` on a malformed bridge result instead of returning `null` or `false`, and `evaluateJavaScript<String>` throws `MonacoProtocolError` for an object or array result instead of returning Dart's `toString()` of it (return `JSON.stringify(...)` from the expression for its JSON text). `MonacoPageConfig.allowedConnectSources` entries are checked against the CSP source-expression grammar: an entry with a query string, a fragment, or `&` (which let an HTML character reference such as `&#59;` add a directive to the policy) now fails `whenReady` with an `ArgumentError`.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:16:- **Options for Monaco 0.56 and 0.57 features.**
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:19:  - `EditorOptions.doubleClickSelectsBlock`: since Monaco 0.56, double-clicking just inside brackets or quotes selects the enclosed block; set `false` to keep plain word selection.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:24:- **Bundled Monaco Editor 0.57.0** (was 0.55.1). Highlights that reach apps without code changes: double-clicking just inside brackets or quotes selects the enclosed block (opt out with `doubleClickSelectsBlock: false`), better IME/EditContext handling, hidden find-widget inputs leave the tab order, and DOMPurify 3.4.15. Markdown from language servers is now untrusted: `command:` links in hovers and completion docs render as plain text.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:26:- **Smaller app footprint for the new engine.** Monaco files no runtime path loads (AMD worker entries and UI translations, 10.6 MB) are left out of the published package, so apps ship about 15 MB of Monaco instead of 25.6 MB.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:27:- **Monaco's MIT license now ships with the package** and appears on apps' license pages; upstream's third-party notices are included under `third_party/monaco-editor/`.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:29:- **`MonacoThemeDefinition.fromJson` requires string `colors` values.** A `null` or numeric color used to become `"null"` or a bare digit string, which Monaco silently painted red; it now throws `FormatException`.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:31:- **Windows: the editor page's origin is `https://flutter-monaco.example`** (see the #43 fix below). Language-server WebSocket handshakes carry it as their `Origin` header.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:62:  - Windows: Monaco's background workers run (#43). `MonacoDiffEditor` shows added and removed lines, and links, word suggestions, and the JSON, CSS, HTML, and TypeScript language services answer. WebView2 does not let a worker load scripts from a `file://` page, so the editor page is now served from the WebView2 virtual host `https://flutter-monaco.example/`, mapped onto the extracted assets. If the WebView2 runtime cannot map the host, or `allowedConnectSources` lists a `ws://` or `http://` endpoint that is not on loopback or a bare `*` (an https page may not reach such endpoints), the page loads from `file://` as before.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:63:  - A WebView that cannot start workers from a `file://` page no longer leaves Monaco waiting on them: the diff is computed on the main thread, and the built-in language services return no result at once instead of hanging. `window.__FM_WORKERS.mode` reports which mode the page runs in. Android, iOS, and macOS keep their real workers.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:71:- **Firefox can now load the editor on Web.** Firefox does not resolve CSP `'self'` to the creating document's origin inside `blob:` documents, so the blob-hosted editor page blocked its own loader, bridge scripts, stylesheet, and workers, failing with "Failed to load Monaco loader.js" while Chrome worked. The page no longer relies on `'self'` for anything it fetches: it names the origin of every resolved asset root explicitly. Native platforms keep a byte-identical policy, and browsers where `'self'` already matches are unaffected.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:72:- **A load blocked by the page's Content-Security-Policy now names the directive that refused it and the URL it refused**, instead of reporting only "Failed to load Monaco loader.js".
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:77:- **Optional package-specific AI assistant support for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex.** A repository-hosted plugin provides six focused skills for integration, 2.x-to-3.x migration, diagnostics, LSP configuration, Dart-to-JavaScript bridge maintenance, and bundled Monaco upgrades. A narrow read-only bridge contract reviewer, deterministic extension validator, and selection/execution/negative/failure eval cases keep the guidance maintainable without adding hooks, services, runtime dependencies, credentials, or published package bulk.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:102:- **Web: the editor pane no longer turns into the browser's "It may have been moved, edited, or deleted." error page.** The Monaco page's blob URL was revoked as soon as the page first reported ready, so any later engine-driven iframe re-insertion reloaded a dead URL. The blob URL now lives exactly as long as the iframe and is released on `dispose()`.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:120:- **`executeAction` waits for asynchronous actions.** The bridge reported success immediately even when the Monaco action returned a promise; failures from async actions now reach Dart.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:136:- **`MonacoDiffController.getLineChangeCount` is loud about an uncomputed diff:** when Monaco has not finished computing (throttled/offscreen views) it throws `MonacoTimeoutError` instead of silently returning `0`, so zero always means a real "no changes" result. `diff.getState` reports the pending state as a `null` count.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:150:- Web: a cross-origin CDN `assetBase` is documented as unsupported for the Monaco assets - the generated page's CSP (`script-src 'self'`) blocks cross-origin bundles; serve flutter_monaco's assets same-origin.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:155:- **`MonacoAssets.precache()`: warm Monaco before the first editor mounts.** On web it fetches the AMD loader, `editor.main.js`/`.css`, and the hash-named editor chunk (~3.6MB, discovered from `editor.main.js` at runtime so it survives Monaco upgrades) into the browser's HTTP cache; the first editor boot is then served from cache instead of starting a multi-megabyte download at mount time. Best-effort and boot-path-untouched: a failed warmup just means the editor downloads the files itself as before. On native platforms it is equivalent to `ensureReady()` (asset extraction). Fire-and-forget from `main()` is the intended use. The README's new "Web performance" section also documents an `index.html` snippet (used by the live demo) that starts the warmup in parallel with the Flutter engine download itself.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:163:- **Web: flaky "Monaco Editor did not report ready in 20 seconds" on cold-cache first loads.** The default `readyTimeout` was a fixed 20 seconds on every platform, but on web the first (uncached) visit must download the multi-megabyte Monaco bundle over the network - a bandwidth-bound wait, not a hang - so slow connections and just-deployed sites (invalidated CDN caches) tripped the deadline mid-download; a retry then succeeded from the warm browser cache. The default is now platform-aware via `MonacoDefaults.readyTimeout` (20s on native, 90s on web). Hard failures (missing assets, script errors) still surface immediately on every platform; the deadline only backstops silent stalls. The web timeout message now also explains the slow-connection case. Explicitly passed `readyTimeout` values behave exactly as before.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:171:- **Multi-document: the boot document no longer dies on the first `activateDocument`.** Monaco's standalone editor takes ownership of a model created implicitly from the `value`/`language` create options and disposes it on the first `setModel`; the boot page now creates the initial model explicitly, so switching documents and back preserves the original document.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:183:- **`EditorOptions` is sparse**: every field is nullable, and `updateOptions(EditorOptions(fontSize: 16))` changes only the font size instead of resetting ~40 options to package defaults. `padding` is `MonacoPadding`, `minimap` is `MonacoMinimapOptions`, `wordWrap`/`lineNumbers` are enums, and structured `scrollbar`/`guides`/`stickyScroll` sub-options plus an `extra` map cover the rest of Monaco's option surface.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:211:- The bridge JavaScript ships as real asset files (`assets/monaco/bridge/*.js`) instead of a Dart string literal, and the generated HTML is rewritten on every load - a package upgrade can never serve a stale bridge, and the manual cache-bust constant is gone.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:222:- **Language Server Protocol support.** `MonacoController.connectLanguageServer` connects the editor to a real language server through Monaco 0.55's built-in LSP client; once connected, completions, hover, go-to-definition, references, rename, formatting, code actions, folding, inlay hints, semantic tokens, and diagnostics come straight from the server with nothing to wire up in Dart. The returned `LanguageServerConnection` exposes `state`/`stateChanges`/`whenClosed`, `disconnect()`, and experimental `sendRequest`/`sendNotification` escape hatches for non-standard server extensions. `disconnectLanguageServer`, `languageServerConnections`, and `languageServerConnection(id)` round out the controller API.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:229:- Opt-in **edge scroll handoff** for editors embedded in scrollable pages. With `MonacoEditor(scrollHandoff: MonacoScrollHandoff.edge(...))`, wheel or trackpad scrolling keeps moving Monaco until the editor reaches its scroll edge (or the document has nothing to scroll), then continues into a configured `ScrollController` or the nearest enclosing vertical `Scrollable`; reversing direction hands the wheel back to the editor. Disabled by default: existing apps keep the exact previous scroll-trapping behavior. Ctrl/meta wheel (editor zoom, browser zoom, macOS pinch) and Monaco's own scrollable overlays (suggest list, hover docs, menus, peek editors) are never handed off, and `scrollBeyondLastLine` blank space counts as editor-scrollable. This is edge handoff across the WebView bridge, not native nested scrolling.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:232:- An experimental, separately opt-in touch source (`MonacoScrollHandoff.edge(mobileTouch: true)`). Touch forwarding is observation-only (it never blocks Monaco's touch handling, never opens the keyboard, and yields to text selection) and has no native momentum or fling transfer.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:236:- Upgraded the bundled Monaco Editor from 0.54.0 to 0.55.1 (first version to ship `monaco.lsp`). Extracted assets re-extract once on first launch after upgrading. The deprecated `monaco.languages.json/css/html/typescript` namespaces are still aliased by Monaco, and the bridge's JSON diagnostics configuration now prefers the new top-level `monaco.json` namespace, so existing code and raw-JS integrations keep working.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:237:- Removed a stray `debugger;` statement from the bundled Monaco 0.55.1 LSP diagnostics feature (an upstream build artifact) so opening the web inspector while an LSP connection starts no longer pauses the editor.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:241:- Mobile web: disposing an editor no longer leaks its Monaco instance. The viewport-fit and keyboard-baseline listeners the editor document registers on the host page's `visualViewport`/window survived `dispose()` (removing an iframe fires no `pagehide`), keeping the whole dead editor document - Monaco included - reachable from the host page. Parent-side listeners now self-detach once the frame leaves the DOM, are all detached eagerly on `dispose()`, and the load-retry path no longer leaks the keyboard-baseline listener either.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:247:- Flutter Web: disabling editor interaction now returns the keyboard to Flutter, not just the pointer. `setInteractionEnabled(false)` (and the `MonacoFocusGuard` route-overlay path that calls it) previously made the iframe pointer-inert and blurred Monaco's textarea, but the parent document's focus stayed ON the iframe element, so every key event kept dispatching inside the iframe: Escape could not close a dialog shown over the editor, Tab could not traverse it, and a button-only alert stayed keyboard-dead until its first click. The interaction toggle now performs the same two-sided handoff as the desktop platforms: blur inside the iframe, then move the parent document's focus onto the editor's own `<flutter-view>` host (multi-view safe, `tabindex` fallback, no scroll jump), so Flutter overlays receive keys immediately. `MonacoController.releaseNativeInputFocus()` performs the same handoff on web instead of being a no-op.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:255:- Fixed Flutter Web WASM compatibility metadata by moving native-only Monaco asset extraction behind conditional storage helpers. Web builds no longer import `path_provider` through `MonacoAssets`, while native platforms keep the same asset extraction behavior.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:260:- Added a macOS native focus plugin that performs the real NSWindow first-responder handoff between the Flutter view and the editor's WKWebView. Clicking Monaco now restores typing through the same native mechanism that made right-click "wake the editor up", instead of an in-page focus replay. The package registers as a plugin on macOS; run your app's usual build (CocoaPods integration is automatic) after upgrading.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:270:- Fixed desktop editor input recovery after Flutter text fields or dialogs leave a stale text-input client active before Monaco is focused.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:278:- Fixed macOS WKWebView input readiness recovery when Monaco appears focused but typing and paste are ignored.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:288:- Mobile Safari on Flutter Web: touch scrolling inside the editor no longer pans the host page (#11). The generated editor document and the host iframe statically declare `touch-action: none` and `overscroll-behavior: none`, so touches that Monaco does not claim can no longer chain out of the frame.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:290:- iOS/macOS worker bootstrap: the WKWebView worker shim now emits escaped newline sequences inside JavaScript string literals, so Monaco language workers load instead of falling back to the main thread.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:295:- **Flutter Web: Monaco failed to load under path URL strategy (#14).** With `usePathUrlStrategy()` (or any non-root route such as GoRouter `/canvas/:id`), the bundled `vs/` URL was built from the browser route, so `loader.js` 404'd and the editor surfaced "Failed to load Monaco loader.js". Asset URLs now resolve through Flutter's asset manager against the document `<base href>`, independent of the current route - so Monaco loads correctly under deep routes, a sub-path `<base href>`, and a CDN `assetBase`.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:303:- **Reliable macOS background.** New `setHostPageBackgroundColor` recolors Monaco's HTML host page. Widget `backgroundColor` applies to both native and host-page layers.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:317:- Fixed Android Flutter Web scroll gestures so scrolling focused Monaco content no longer opens the keyboard on release, while preserving intentional keyboard-open scrolling.
./packages/flutter_monaco/CHANGELOG.md:318:- Fixed a Flutter Web first-load race by waiting for iframe attachment and retrying transient Monaco load failures.
